text:
priya: FYI during the staged quota rollout this morning we saw repeated short-term "thrashing" where agents alternated between two weight sets and a few tenants dropped below their p50.
michael: saw traces. looks like agents accepted a diff, then rolled it back when they couldn't fetch a missing base snapshot.
tess: root cause seems to be ambiguous contract: current policy push is "best-effort diff" with no replay guarantees. if an agent misses the base we get half-applied state.
dan: do we want to fix by making the transport reliable or by changing the data model to be snapshot-first?
priya: lean toward snapshot-first with a lightweight handshake so agents can request incremental diffs only when they have the base. reduces complexity of repair.
michael: agreed. idea: handshake -> agent sends current policy_version, policy-service responds with either {delta} or {full_snapshot, version}.
tess: propose proto sketch: 
```
message AgentHello { string agent_id = 1; string current_version = 2; }
message PolicyResponse { enum Type { DELTA=0; SNAPSHOT=1; } Type type = 1; string version = 2; bytes payload = 3; }
```
priya: and a rule: agent must not apply a delta whose base_version != agent.current_version. policy-service must return snapshot in that case.
dan: we should also include monotonic sequence numbers and a signed checksum in the header so we can detect silent corruption.
michael: another operational concern: rollout speed. if policy-service floods agents with snapshots it will overload network. need a backoff/queue with advertised capacity per-agent.
tess: right. add an admission header: {queue_limit, preferred_backoff_ms}. agent will advertise apply_capacity during handshake.
priya: on abuse signals: currently abuse-detector writes annotations to policy-service which then mutates weights. that coupling causes delays. suggest we allow short-circuit emergency hints directly to local agents (no weight mutation allowed) so they can temporarily soft-shed.
dan: must be constrained: local agents get capability flags in the handshake like [soft_shed, throttle_hint], and any local action must post an audit event to policy-service within X seconds.
michael: and audit events should be signed and include evidence (sampled request ids + pre-admission telemetry) so policy-service can validate.
tess: we should avoid letting noisy detectors cause cascade. define threshold semantics and cooldowns on local emergency actions.
priya: for backwards compatibility: policy-service supports v1 push-diffs and v2 handshake/snapshot. agents declare supported_versions in AgentHello. server can downgrade.
dan: telemetry: per-agent snapshot_lag, applied_version, emergency_actions_count, rejected_deltas. add into Console dashboards.
michael: test plan: 1) simulate dropped packets during rollout, assert convergence within T; 2) aggressive abuse-signal storm, ensure local soft-shed triggers but is audited and reversible.
tess: timeline: short fix = require delta checksums and reject deltas if base mismatch (2 days). medium = handshake + snapshot fallback (3 weeks). long = full admission/fairness/abuse split with capability registry and signed audit pipeline (Q2).
priya: action items: tess to write proto sketch + compatibility matrix, michael to prototype handshake server behavior, dan to spec audit event schema, i'll add tests for chaos rollouts.
ops-bot: deploy note: canary v2-rollout-3 -> 04:00-05:30; monitoring: increased policy push retries logged.
priya: quick note: keep emergency local actions strictly advisory for hosted customers, for dedicated/private we can allow more aggressive overrides but still require operator opt-in.
dan: good call. also add ACLs to the capability flags so only approved builds get soft_shed.
michael: will start a PR for proto files and an integration test harness.
tess: logging item: include the handshake exchange in trace spans so we can debug mismatches in the future.
priya: thanks all, i'll follow up with a brief RFC summary and a proposed field list for the Console telemetry.
ops-bot: reminder: eng-platform sync Friday 14:00 GMT
priya: closing thread, reopen if anything else pops up.
